title: Add-On Charges on an Active Patient Payment Plan
content:
**Financial counseling desk guidance — adding new charges to a Patient Payment Plan**

**Rule A1.** Add-ons are accepted only on a Patient Payment Plan in active status. The status is the one shown on that agreement's record before the charge is added.

**Rule A2.** Where the tier allows add-ons, an eligible new charge is added while the plan's add-on count is below the tier's limit of add-ons per plan and the plan balance after the add-on stays within the tier's largest balance. A charge that would take the balance beyond that figure starts no new plan and stays on its plan of care.

**Rule A3.** The add-on count is the number of distinct dates on which charges were added on to the plan over its whole life.

**Rule A4.** The tier's add-on method decides how the add-on is absorbed: under "recalculate payment" the installment is recomputed over the remaining months; under "extend term" the installment stays and months are added, never more than the tier's maximum term extension in total.

## Decision table

| Plan status | Tier allows add-ons | Add-on count below the tier's limit | Balance after the add-on within the tier's largest balance | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Active | Yes | Yes | Yes | The charge is added (Rule A2) |
| Active | Yes | Yes | No | No new plan; the charge stays on its plan of care |
| Pending signature, past due, defaulted, paid off or cancelled | — | — | — | Not accepted as an add-on (Rule A1) |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- Two eligible charges are added to an active plan on the same day. Under Rule A3 they count as one add-on.
- An active plan on a tier whose largest balance is 1500.00 has a balance of 1420.00; a new eligible charge of 95.00 would take it to 1515.00, beyond the figure. The charge stays on its plan of care and no new plan is started for it.
- Under "extend term", a plan already extended by months up to the tier's maximum term extension in total takes no further months.
